GDP, (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026
items.summary: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.

items.title: Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026
items.summary: Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)–personal income less personal current taxes–increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent). Personal outlays–the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments–increased $69.3 billion in October. Personal saving was $1.00 trillion, and the personal saving rate–personal saving as a percentage of DPI–was 4.1 percent.

items.title: Activities of U.S. Multinational Enterprises, 2024
items.summary: Worldwide employment by U.S. multinational enterprises increased 0.9 percent to 44.2 million workers in 2024 (preliminary) from 43.8 million workers in 2023 (revised), according to statistics released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis on the operations and finances of U.S. parent companies and their majority-owned foreign affiliates.

items.title: Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025
items.summary: The value added of the outdoor recreation economy accounted for 2.3 percent ($704.2 billion) of current-dollar gross domestic product (GDP) for the nation in 2025. Across states and the District of Columbia, value added for outdoor recreation as a share of state GDP ranged from 6.1 percent in Hawaii to 1.0 percent in the District of Columbia.
